Hi Cleo —

Following up ahead of your renewal in December. Attached is a short usage health pack that covers: token cadence (Q3→Q4), 95/99 latency percentiles on your primary chat route, and a couple of modeled term options that could lower unit costs if you adopt a T+1 rolling billing cadence. High-level items:

- Peak daily footprint this quarter: 7.2M tokens (5% of requests hit our secondary larger-context model).
- Latency: median 220ms, p95 540ms (we've flagged a tail on burst windows at 11:30–12:30 PT).

Options included in the PDF: 
A) 12-month renewal (baseline): keep same vCPUs/GPU mix; nominal per-token price.
B) 12-month w/ T+1 cadence: commit to a rolling monthly true-up that smooths monthly overages, enabling us to reduce per-token by ~9% for sustained higher cadence.
C) 24-month commitment with staged capacity discounts (uses reserved Dedicated lanes for predictable throughput).

I called out likely operational wins if you enable prefix caching for your user-facing composer (we modeled ~15% token reduction for repetitive assistant prompts; see the Excel).

Can we schedule a 30-minute run-through next week to pick an option? Rachel and Vivek are on cc for the modeling and pricing details.

Thanks,
—Lauren

Lauren / Vivek —

Quick notes from the modeling side: 
- The 9% per-token reduction is applied to normalized monthly token consumption after true-up. Spikes are treated as overage and reconciled in the next month; for one-off spikes under 30% above baseline we proposed a one-time credit smoothing (call it protection band).
- The p95 tail looks correlated to cache miss rate on the assistant route (their prefix cache hit ~18% today). If they enable prefix caching on the top 3 templates we expect hit to climb to ~45% which yields the modeled 12–16% token reduction and helps the p95 by ~80–140ms in our staging runs.
- Pricing sensitivity: if they commit to T+1 we can push a 9% unit price cut; if they commit to 24 months we can tier discounts up to 16% depending on committed MTU.

I’ll bring the scenario worksheet to the meeting.

-rachel

Also recommend we flag the prefix-cache config as a customer task in the mutual action plan; include a short checklist and a stub PR template for their engineers.
